custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create a tracked part, part A, for this test, with 4 on hand at a Cost of $12.50, so its stock is worth $50.00 (4 × $12.50).
  • Set part A inactive.
  • Start on the Inventory Value report (Reports in the top bar, then Inventory Value), for today at the test location.

How to set this up on the QA site (https://sv10647.qa.shopview.com):

  • Admin at the test location: on the QA site's sign-in screen choose Admin. The test location is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919; its name shows in the box at the top right. If another name shows, click that box, click the name beside Change Location: and pick Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • To create a part: click Parts in the top bar, Inventory in the left menu, then New Inventory Part. Fill Description and Part Number (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-C425756-A for part A, -B for part B), pick a Category, type a Cost and a Sell Price, type the Quantity in the bin row (the location's bin, for example General Storage, is offered), then click Save. Leave Track quantities and cost of goods on for a tracked part; click it off for an untracked part. Add Bin Location adds a second bin; Vendor, Manufacturer, Core Charge, Min, Max and Tags are in the same window. Parts that must start with the same text all start ZZAUTOTEST-PL-C425756-, so searching for that finds them all.
  • The Search box above the Inventory list opens when you click Search (the magnifier).
  • To set a part inactive: on the Inventory page's Active tab click Search, type its part number, click its row; in Edit Inventory Part click Inactive under Part Status, click Save, then click Deactivate in the Deactivate part? window. The part then shows on the Inactive tab.
  • The Inventory Value report: Reports in the top bar, then Inventory Value. Its As of: date, Category:, Vendor: and Location: filters sit above the table; Download (PDF) and Download (CSV) are in its three-dot menu.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Part A is listed with Qty 4, Unit Cost $12.50 and Total Cost $50.00 (4 × $12.50): an inactive part's stock still has value.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10822 (Story 9, Inactive Parts Cannot Be Added to New Work)

  • S9-E11: “Reports keep inactive parts. Inventory Value and Parts Velocity include them, because their stock still has value and their history still happened.”
  • Feature Overview, Accounting: “Setting a part inactive does not touch stock, cost of goods or QuickBooks.”
